name: Ajanta Caves
summary: Rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments featuring world-famous ancient fresco paintings and sculptures.
description: Dating from the 2nd century BCE to about 480 CE, the 30 rock-cut caves present masterpieces of Buddhist religious art.

name: Ellora Caves & Kailasa Temple
summary: Colossal multi-religious rock-hewn monolithic temple complex, featuring the famous Cave 16 Kailasa temple.
description: Carved out of the Charanandri hills between the 6th and 10th century CE, featuring Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain sanctuaries.

name: Gateway of India
summary: Iconic arch-monument overlooking the Arabian Sea, built in Indo-Saracenic style.
description: Erected to commemorate the landing of King George V and Queen Mary in 1911, completed in 1924.

name: Tiger's Point (Tiger's Leap)
summary: Dramatic 650-meter cliff-top viewpoint resembling a leaping tiger into the valley, famous for echo point and rolling Sahyadri clouds.
description: Perched high above the valley in Kurvande near Lonavala, Tiger's Leap offers stunning sheer drop views of the Western Ghats, waterfalls, and mist-covered mountain valleys.

name: Bhushi Dam & Cascades
summary: Historic 1860s masonry dam on the Indrayani River, world-famous for its stepped waterfalls and gushing monsoon cascades.
description: Constructed in the late 1860s for the Great Indian Peninsula Railway to supply water to steam locomotives, Bhushi Dam is Lonavala's most beloved monsoon tourist hotspot.

name: Karla Caves (Grand Chaitya Hall)
summary: Ancient 2nd-century BCE rock-cut Buddhist shrine with India's largest Chaitya hall, original 2,200-year-old teak wood ribs and lion pillars.
description: An archaeological marvel carved into the rocky hill at Karli, Karla Caves house the largest early Buddhist rock-cut prayer hall in India with 37 majestic octagonal pillars and the sacred Ekvira Temple.

name: Bhaja Caves & Waterfall
summary: Group of 22 rock-cut Buddhist caves from 2nd century BCE featuring wooden architecture carvings, a dancing woman relief, and 14 stupas.
description: Perched 400 feet above the village of Bhaja near Lonavala, this monastic complex features extraordinary Buddhist reliefs, ancient Hinayana stupas, and a seasonal monsoon waterfall cascade.

name: Lohagad Fort (The Iron Fortress)
summary: Historic Maratha hilltop fortress at 1,033m elevation, fortified by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, featuring the famous Vinchukata spur.
description: Lohagad (Iron Fort) divides the Indrayani and Pavana basins. It has four formidable gates—Ganesh Darwaja, Narayan Darwaja, Hanuman Darwaja, and Maha Darwaja—and the iconic 1,500m scorpion-tail fortified ridge.

name: Rajmachi Fort & Sahyadri Plateau
summary: Historic twin forts (Shrivardhan and Manaranjan) guarding the ancient Borghat pass, famous for lush trekking, views, and fireflies.
description: Standing strategically in the rugged Sahyadri mountains between Khandala and Karjat, Rajmachi Fort comprises two citadel fortresses offering breathtaking vistas of the Ulhas river valley and Duke's Nose.

name: Duke's Nose (Nagphani Peak)
summary: Dramatic cliff peak shaped like a cobra's hood offering thrilling rock climbing, rappelling, and 360-degree Sahyadri valley views.
description: Also known as Nagphani due to its resemblance to a cobra's raised hood, the peak was nicknamed Duke's Nose by British surveyors. It is renowned for its sheer vertical drop and sweeping views of the Khandala ghats.

name: Khandala Sunset Point (Amrutanjan Ghat)
summary: Celebrated scenic vantage point over the deep Bhor Ghat valley and Duke's Nose, famous for spectacular sunsets and cloud phenomena.
description: Located near the historic Amrutanjan Bridge on the old Mumbai-Pune highway, this iconic viewpoint provides expansive vistas of lush valleys, train tunnels cutting through mountains, and golden sunsets.

name: Kune Waterfalls (Three-Tier Cascade)
summary: India's 14th highest waterfall dropping 200 meters in three majestic tiers amid dense Sahyadri greenery.
description: Nestled in the lush greenery between Khandala and Lonavala, Kune Falls plunges 660 feet into a rocky basin against the backdrop of the Sahyadri mountains, creating an unforgettable monsoon spectacle.

name: Lion's Point Viewpoint
summary: High-altitude vantage point between Bhushi Dam and Aamby Valley, known for soaring wind currents and panoramic mountain gorges.
description: Situated midway between Bhushi Dam and Aamby Valley, Lion's Point offers sharp cliff drops, winds that lift water droplets upwards, and incredible sunrise and sunset vistas across the Sahyadri range.

name: Pawna Lake & Dam Reserve
summary: Expansive freshwater reservoir framed by Lohagad, Tikona and Tung forts; premier destination for lakeside camping and kayaking.
description: Surrounded by historic Maratha fortresses, Pawna Lake offers calm waters, picturesque lakeside campsites, bonfire evenings, and water sports just 20 km from central Lonavala.

name: Sunil's Celebrity Wax Museum
summary: Pioneering Indian wax museum housing lifelike statues of historic leaders, scientists, freedom fighters, and cricket icons.
description: Founded by wax sculptor Sunil Kandalloor, this popular indoor museum features detailed life-size figures of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam, Mahatma Gandhi, and global figures.
